problem_text:
A logistics firm is preparing a cargo shipment for an intercontinental air freight service. The company must select a combination of crates to maximize total revenue while adhering to the aircraft's maximum payload capacity.

The available crates are:
* Crate 1: mass 15kg, revenue 167 units
* Crate 2: mass 22kg, revenue 278 units
* Crate 3: mass 19kg, revenue 150 units
* Crate 4: mass 25kg, revenue 258 units
* Crate 5: mass 8kg, revenue 49 units
* Crate 6: mass 27kg, revenue 110 units
* Crate 7: mass 42kg, revenue 99 units
* Crate 8: mass 44kg, revenue 116 units
* Crate 9: mass 18kg, revenue 200 units
* Crate 10: mass 42kg, revenue 278 units
* Crate 11: mass 29kg, revenue 235 units
* Crate 12: mass 45kg, revenue 219 units
* Crate 13: mass 14kg, revenue 287 units
* Crate 14: mass 29kg, revenue 185 units
* Crate 15: mass 7kg, revenue 121 units
* Crate 16: mass 40kg, revenue 254 units
* Crate 17: mass 20kg, revenue 63 units
* Crate 18: mass 2kg, revenue 26 units
* Crate 19: mass 5kg, revenue 129 units
* Crate 20: mass 36kg, revenue 226 units
* Crate 21: mass 42kg, revenue 174 units
* Crate 22: mass 33kg, revenue 58 units
* Crate 23: mass 6kg, revenue 257 units
* Crate 24: mass 19kg, revenue 263 units
* Crate 25: mass 30kg, revenue 40 units
* Crate 26: mass 20kg, revenue 287 units
* Crate 27: mass 42kg, revenue 291 units

Furthermore, due to contractual obligations, precisely one of Crate 1 and Crate 2 must be included in the shipment.

Should Crate 3 be selected, the effective payload capacity of the aircraft is diminished by 10 kg.
The aircraft can accommodate a maximum of 476 kg. The firm must determine which crates to load.
